_doc: pc/tools/ps1_source_edits.py: calls whose argument from the fifth on is passed as a 4-byte integer where the callee's definition reads an 8-byte pointer (pc/tools/audit_ps1_call_args.py --width: WIN64-STACK, the fifth and sixth arguments, on the stack only in the Microsoft x64 convention; STACK-WIDTH, the seventh on, on the stack on Linux too).  The caller stores 4 bytes into the 8-byte slot and the callee reads the slot's stale upper half.  Each entry passes the argument as a zero-extended 64-bit value (u64), the console's 32-bit address; the callee is not changed.  A HAL callee is fixed in the HAL instead (pc/hal/gpu.c SetDrawMode).  edits: [old, new(, count)] exact replacements, line count kept.  A stale entry stops the build.  docs/pc-port/WINDOWS-BUILD.md "Calling convention".

main/GsSortObject4.why: the libgs divide-mode dispatch calls GsTMDdiv{NF3,NF4,TNF3,NG3,TNG3,NG4,TNF4,TNG4} with the ordering-table context (arg1, an s32 PS1 address) and the work area (arg3, s32 *) as the sixth and seventh arguments through `s32` prototypes; the definitions (src/main/matched/GsTMDdiv*.c) read `OtCtx *ctx` / `Work *work`.  Windows found it (WIN64-STACK x8); the seventh is on the stack on Linux too (STACK-WIDTH x8).

KANGEI/kangei_msg_disp4.why: msg_str_disp(x, y, color, str, arg4, suffix, bullet, show) reads suffix and bullet as u8 * (src/main/matched/msg_str_disp.c, K&R); kangei_msg_disp4 passes `(s32)&kangei_msg4_suf_str` and `(s32)&kangei_msg4_bul_str` through an all-s32 prototype: the sixth (WIN64-STACK) and seventh (STACK-WIDTH) arguments.  The module calls it unprototyped (generate_overlay_modules.py's canonical `extern s32 msg_str_disp();`), so the values are passed as u64 explicitly.

main/TmdF3.why: TmdF3 forwards its own s32 arg6/arg7 (the ordering-table context and the work area) to the unprototyped GsTMDdiv*L / *LFG / *NL renderers, whose definitions read them as pointers (OtCtx *ctx / Work *work, or GsOT *ot / GsWORK *w): the seventh and eighth arguments, on the stack on Linux and Windows alike (STACK-WIDTH x6).
edits: (a0, a1, a2, a3, arg4, arg5, arg6, arg7);
